title: From IceCube to IT-Sphere: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical GNN for Banking IT Root Cause Analysis
authors: Antonio Greco, Riccardo Paoletti, Roberto Cappuccio, Mario Onorato
abstract: We present Hybrid Quantum Root Cause Analysis (HQ-RCA), an industrially grounded workflow for root cause analysis in banking IT operations, built on a hybrid Quantum Graph Neural Network (QGNN): the classical backbone of DynEdge (the IceCube neutrino-reconstruction GNN, which we call standalone DynEdge), with its classification head replaced by a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). On 13 months of anonymised IT data (13k alarm clusters) from a major European bank, the hybrid QGNN matches standalone DynEdge -- the strongest classical baseline -- on $F_1$, while standalone DynEdge leads the ranking metrics. A readout-sensitivity and layout-robustness study, analysed via Dimensional Expressivity Analysis (DEA), shows that the effective parameter dimensionality (rank) of the quantum observable has no measurable correlation with $F_1$; we therefore keep the simplest readout $\langle Z_0\rangle$ (the Pauli-$Z$ expectation on the first qubit), which in the deployed layout is rank-1, collapsing optimisation to a 1-D problem solvable by a gradient-free grid scan. Execution on IBM Heron r2 (no error mitigation) shows this gradient-free readout is executable on NISQ hardware after threshold recalibration.
summary: This paper introduces HQ-RCA, a hybrid quantum-classical GNN designed for root cause analysis in banking IT. It integrates a classical GNN (DynEdge) with a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) to process IT alarm data. The model successfully runs on NISQ hardware, showing that while the quantum component is feasible, the classical backbone remains the strongest baseline for certain metrics.
main_problem: The paper addresses root cause analysis (RCA) in complex banking IT systems, framing it as a graph-reconstruction problem.
main_result: The hybrid quantum-classical GNN (HQ-RCA) achieved an F1 score matching the best classical baseline on NISQ hardware, demonstrating feasibility for operational use.
method: A hybrid model combines a classical Graph Neural Network (DynEdge) with a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) acting as the classification head.
model_or_system: The system models the IT ecosystem as the 'IT-Sphere,' analogous to the IceCube neutrino detector. The model uses a QGNN structure, involving classical feature embedding followed by a 4-qubit VQC.
key_observables: F1 score, Area Under the Curve (AP), ROC-AUC, and the Pauli-Z expectation $\langle Z_0 angle$.
important_parameters: The effective parameter dimensionality (rank) of the quantum observable, which was found to be rank-1 for the chosen readout.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the choice of performance metric (F1 vs. AP/AUC) dictates the optimal architectural choice (hybrid head vs. standalone classical model).
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the structural analogy between IceCube and the IT-Sphere; Figure 2 illustrates the end-to-end HQ-RCA workflow, and Figure 3 displays the DEA SVD spectrum confirming rank-1 structure.
paper_structure: The paper details the workflow: classical preprocessing (Union-Find, PCA) $	o$ classical embedding (DynEdge) $	o$ quantum encoding (VQC) $	o$ measurement ($\langle Z_0 angle$) $	o$ final classical readout. Performance is evaluated using various metrics and tested on real NISQ hardware.
why_interesting: The work demonstrates a concrete, near-term application of quantum circuits (VQC) to a complex, real-world data analysis problem, providing empirical evidence of quantum advantage potential in structured data processing.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
